newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to convert Central Bank loans to bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia to convert Central Bank loans to bonds.

text.p: The Russian government intends to convert direct credits lent by the Central Bank to the government in 1992-94 into 80.4 trillion roubles of non-market medium-term fixed rate bonds, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Friday.

The bonds will not be traded initially on the second market, but the Central Bank will have the right to sell them from its portfolio to manage liquidity, Bella Zlatkis, head of the ministry's securities department, told Reuters.
"We decided in this year's budget to bring some order into the debt owed the Central Bank which has been piling up for many years, and restructure it into normal debt," Zlatkis said.
Zlatkis said the ministry and bank had agreed that the bonds would not appear on the market for the time being.

"In principle, these securities can come on to the market only if there is excessive monetary liquidity. But according to the agreement between us and the Central Bank, these securities will not appear on the market for now," she said.
The Central Bank is now banned by law from making direct credits to the government, but in the first years of economic reform it transferred money to fund the budget deficit, helping fuel inflation.

According to Article 74 of the latest draft of the 1997 budget, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, the government and Central Bank will convert 57.1 trillion roubles of credits granted between 1992 and 1994, and 23.3 trillion roubles of interest due on these credits between 1997 and 2004, into 80.4 trillion roubles of fixed-rate OFZ government bonds.
The budget is receiving its fourth and final reading in the State Duma lower house of parliament on Friday.

The bonds, with the usual 1.00 million rouble denomination, will be issued on March 15 this year and repaid in equal yearly tranches from 2001 to 2013 on March 15. They will pay a fixed rate of 10 percent a year, starting in 1998.
